title: Why the Garden Needed Fewer Plants
passage:
Rina joined the school gardening club because she loved flowers. During her first year, the club tried to make every corner of the school garden colorful. Members planted many kinds of flowers close together, believing that more plants would make the garden more beautiful. For a few weeks, the result looked wonderful. By early summer, however, problems appeared. Some plants grew quickly and covered smaller ones. Others became weak because they received too little sunlight or air. Watering also took a long time, and club members often disagreed about which areas needed attention first. The adviser did not tell them what to do. Instead, she asked them to record what was happening. The students measured sunlight in different areas, noted how quickly the soil dried, and checked which flowers attracted insects. They discovered that several plants were competing for the same space, while a few stronger plants were doing well with very little care. Rina was surprised when the adviser suggested removing some healthy plants. It felt wrong to take out flowers that were not sick. Yet the club decided to test the idea in one section. They moved some plants to pots and left more space between the remaining ones. A month later, the test area required less water and had fewer damaged leaves. Bees and butterflies could move more easily between flowers, and students had space to pull weeds without stepping on plants. The club then redesigned the rest of the garden. They used fewer species in each area and chose plants according to sunlight and soil conditions. The garden looked less crowded, but the colors were clearer because each group of plants could be seen. The students also spent less time solving emergency problems and more time observing seasonal changes. Rina learned that caring for something does not always mean adding more. Sometimes improvement comes from reducing competition and giving each part enough space. She later noticed the same idea in other situations. A schedule with too many activities can become hard to manage, and a poster with too many messages can be difficult to read. The garden taught her that limits are not always a weakness. They can help people decide what matters most and create conditions in which the remaining parts can grow better.

The club kept one section of the old crowded design as a comparison. Over several weeks, students recorded how much water each section needed and how many plants became damaged. The crowded section was not always worse; during a short cool period, some plants there stayed moist longer. This reminded Rina that simple rules such as more space is always better can also become misleading. Conditions matter. The club used its records to adjust spacing instead of following one fixed distance for every plant. They also began writing short notes for future members so the reasons behind each choice would not be forgotten. Rina came to see the garden as a changing system rather than a decoration that could be finished once and left alone.
translation:
里奈は花が好きで園芸部に入りました。最初の年、部員たちは学校の庭をできるだけ色鮮やかにしようと、たくさんの種類の花を狭い場所に植えました。最初はきれいでしたが、夏になると成長の速い植物が小さな植物を覆い、日光や風が足りず弱るものが出てきました。水やりにも時間がかかり、どこを優先するかで意見が分かれました。顧問は答えを教える代わりに、まず状況を記録するよう求めました。生徒たちは日当たり、土の乾き方、昆虫が集まる花などを調べ、いくつもの植物が同じ空間を奪い合っていることに気づきました。顧問が健康な植物を一部取り除く案を出したとき、里奈は驚きました。しかし一角で試しに植物を鉢へ移し、間隔を広げると、一か月後には水の量が減り、葉の傷みも少なくなりました。ハチやチョウも動きやすくなり、除草もしやすくなりました。そこで庭全体を見直し、場所ごとに種類を絞り、日当たりや土に合う植物を選びました。以前ほど密集していませんが、むしろ色のまとまりがはっきりしました。里奈は、世話をすることは必ずしも何かを足すことではなく、競争を減らし十分な空間を与えることも改善につながると学びました。そして、予定を詰め込みすぎると管理が難しくなることや、ポスターに情報を入れすぎると読みにくくなることにも同じ考えが当てはまると気づきました。制限は弱点ではなく、大切なものを選び、残したものをよりよく育てるための条件にもなるのです。

部は以前の密集した植え方も一部残し、必要な水量や傷んだ植物の数を比較しました。涼しい時期には密集区の方が土の湿りを保つ場合もあり、『間隔が広いほど常によい』という単純な規則も危険だと分かりました。条件を見ながら間隔を調整し、理由を次の部員へ残すことで、里奈は庭を一度完成させる飾りではなく、変化し続ける仕組みとして見るようになりました。
